newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Sino Land 1995/96 net in line - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Sino Land 1995/96 net in line - analysts.

text.p: Sino Land Co Ltd's 60 percent drop in 1995/96 net profit was in line with expectations, after an exceptional gain of HK$1.92 billion in the 1994/95 financial year boosted earnings in that period, analysts said on Tuesday.

Sino Land posted net profit of HK$1.15 billion for the year ended June 30 versus HK$2.87 billion in the year-ago period. The year-ago period included an exceptional item of HK$1.92 billion from the spin-off the Sino Land's hospitality interests.

"It was a very dull year. They did not sell a lot of property," said Frederick Tsang, head of research at PrimeEast Securities (HK) Ltd. He was expecting a 15 percent increase in profit excluding exceptionals.

"I think the whole market expected a big fall in net profit mainly because of an exceptional gain in 1995 so I don't think that will be a surprise," said one analyst at a Japanese house who was expecting net profit of HK$1.1 billion.
Sino Land said property sales rose 38 percent to HK$1.40 billion in 1995/96 and rental income rose 12 percent to HK$1.09 billion "in spite of highly competitive environment".
"All the stock they sold was previously unsold residential units carried over to the fiscal year ending June 30. There is nothing exciting there," said one analyst.
Tsang said Sino Land had refrained from selling residential units during a downturn in the residential market, contributing to a low level of property sales.

"Over the last few years they completed a lot of luxury residential property. They kept most of them for rental income and also for capital appreciation so that is why over the last couple of years they have built up a sizeable rental portfolio."
"Their strategy turns out to be quite right. Over the last last few months we have witnessed a strong interest in buying land," Tsang added.
Sino Land said its Dynasty View project was completed in the period and will be marketed in 1996/97.

It said gross floor area attributable to the Sino group from sites A, B, and C of the Tai Kok Tsui Mass Transit Railway station amounted to more than 2.1 million square feet "bringing a stream of attractive profits well into the next century".
"We are looking for earnings growth to 1.5 billion (for 1996/97)," the analyst at the Japanese brokerage said.
Tsang said he was expecting more than 20 percent annual earnings growth over the next few years.
Sino Land shares closed at HK$8.45 on Tuesday, steady compared to Monday's close.
